successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Epirus after 'Molossia fell to Rome in 167 BC'

ledger.x: ~370: the Molossian Aeacidae found the first centralized state in Epirus.
343/2: Philip II makes Alexander king of Epirus.
334: Alexander of Epirus crosses to Italy 'at the request of the Greek colony of Taras' and takes Heraclea from the Lucanians.
334: Terina from the Bruttii ('He then took Heraclea from the Lucanians, Terina from the Bruttii, and Sipontum on the Adriatic coast').
334: Sipontum on the Adriatic coast; the page does not name the owner (Italic tribes).
ledger.cp: Italic tribes (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 331: Alexander of Epirus 'was compelled to engage under unfavourable circumstances in the Battle of Pandosia and was killed by a Lucanian'.
331: the Macedonian-installed king dies; the page says nothing of Epirus's later relation to Macedon (bridging end of the client relation).
330: the Epirote tribes unite.
295: Pyrrhus moves the capital from Passaron to Ambracia.
295: Ambracia is in the kingdom (the capital is moved there).
ledger.cp: Ambracia (previous holder not named on the page)

ledger.x: 288: Pyrrhus shares Macedonia.
284: Lysimachus drives Pyrrhus out.
280: Pyrrhus lands in Italy at Tarentum's request ('The Tarentines asked Pyrrhus to lead their war against the Romans' ...
277: Pyrrhus takes Eryx in Sicily.
275: Beneventum ends the Italian and Sicilian adventure.
274: Pyrrhus seizes the Macedonian throne.
272: Pyrrhus is killed in a street battle at Argos ('Pyrrhus was killed during a street battle at Argos'); the page does not say when Antigonus recovered Macedonia (bridging).
272: Pyrrhus dies; the page is silent on the end of Tarentum's dominion (bridging).
231: the monarchy is abolished and Epirus becomes a federal republic.
After the monarchy: 'the Aetolians seized Ambracia, Amphilochia, and land north of the Ambracian Gulf.'
224: the capital moves to Phoenice.
167: Rome ends Epirus.

wars.name: Italian campaign of Alexander I of Epirus
wars.outcome: Alexander took Heraclea, Terina and Sipontum and was killed at Pandosia (331); the page does not say what happened to the towns.

wars.name: Macedonian wars of Pyrrhus
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus co-ruled Macedon with Lysimachus from 288, was driven out in 284, seized the throne from Antigonus Gonatas in 274 and died at Argos in 272.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus won at Heraclea (280) and Asculum (279, 'at a high cost'), took Eryx in 277, and 'lost all his gains after the Battle of Beneventum in 275 BC'; Tarentum stayed under Epirote dominion.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War (end)
wars.outcome: 'Molossia fell to Rome in 167 BC'; Epirus conquered by the Roman Republic.

certainty.note: No page dates a frontier of Epirus; the borders (Aetolian League to the south, Thessaly and Upper Macedonia to the east, Illyrian tribes to the north) are approximate throughout; the Italian and Sicilian holdings are points, not frontiers.
